rows.head: Lohrei sparks a Bruins comeback
rows.story: Anton Frondell struck first for the Blackhawks on the power play early in the first, with Patrick Kane picking up his 900th NHL assist on the goal. David Pastrňák made it 1-1 for Boston midway through the period. Frondell scored his second of the night early in the second to put the Hawks back ahead 2-1.

chips: First goal for a new club
rows.head: Snuggerud sparks the Blues back from two down
rows.story: Dalibor Dvorský got the scoring started for the Blues early in the first. The Blues went more than 26 minutes without a shot on goal, from early in the first to midway through the second, even with a power play in that stretch. Most teams don’t go that long without a shot even once a season.

rows.head: Luukkonen steals one in Los Angeles
rows.story: Jack Quinn struck first for the Sabres on the power play early in the first, and Tage Thompson made it 2-0 late in the second. Corey Perry got the Kings on the board on the power play less than two minutes later. Andre Lee tied it up early in the third, but that was the last goal the Kings would get.

rows.head: Stamkos seals it in the shootout
rows.story: Reid Schaefer got the scoring started for the Predators midway through the first, but John Carlson tied it up for Tampa Bay less than three minutes later. It was a busy second period. Jake Guentzel gave the Lightning the lead just 18 seconds into the period, but Adam Edström made it 2-2 for Nashville just 45 seconds into the period.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: Anderson has two goals and an assist as the Canadiens get past the Penguins
rows.story: The first period was a wild one. Erik Karlsson opened the scoring for the Penguins on the power play early in the period. Oliver Kapanen and Josh Anderson scored 24 seconds apart later in the period to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: Blueger scores in his return to Vancouver
rows.story: William Nylander struck first for the Maple Leafs less than two minutes in, but Brock Boeser made it 1-1 for Vancouver on the power play midway through the first. Auston Matthews put the Leafs ahead for good early in the second. Zack MacEwen made it 3-1 midway through the period, and that one stood up as the winner.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: The Stars get past the Blue Jackets
rows.story: Mikko Rantanen got the scoring started for the Stars on the power play early in the first. Thomas Harley made it 2-0 with just one second left in the period, and that one stood up as the winner. The Blue Jackets’ Erik Gudbranson didn’t play after 16:38 of the second period.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: Jarry blanks the Islanders
rows.story: Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Vasily Podkolzin scored just over a minute apart midway through the second to put the Oilers up 2-0. Nugent-Hopkins struck again on the power play late in the period to make it 3-0. Jason Dickinson added an empty-net goal with less than three minutes left to make it 4-0.
rows.calls: Two of four preview calls held

rows.head: Four points for Cale Makar as the Avalanche beat the Flames
rows.story: Nathan MacKinnon got the scoring started for the Avalanche midway through the first. It was a busy second period. Martin Nečas, Artturi Lehkonen and Brock Nelson scored three goals in less than seven minutes early in the period to stretch the lead to 4-0.
rows.calls: Two of four preview calls held

rows.head: The Senators cruise past the Sharks
rows.story: Dylan Cozens got the scoring started for the Senators midway through the first. Michael Misa tied it 1-1 for San Jose less than three minutes later, but the Sharks didn’t score again. Drake Batherson restored the Senators’ lead early in the second, and Tim Stützle made it 3-1 midway through the period.
rows.calls: One of three preview calls held

rows.head: Drysdale has three assists as the Flyers beat the Mammoth
rows.story: Matvei Michkov got the scoring started for the Flyers midway through the first, but Dmitri Simashev made it 1-1 for Utah a minute and a half later. Travis Konecny restored the Flyers’ lead early in the second, in his first game back after missing ten games. Noah Cates made it 3-1 less than five minutes later.
rows.calls: Two of three preview calls held

rows.head: Nothing gets past Kochetkov
rows.story: An ugly night for the Jets. Sean Walker, who scores in about 1 game in 11, scored twice. Walker opened the scoring for the Hurricanes shorthanded early in the first.
rows.calls: Two of four preview calls held

rows.head: Kaprizov reaches 500 points as the Wild beat the Capitals
rows.story: David Špaček picked up his first NHL point. Quinn Hughes and Michael McCarron scored less than two minutes apart early in the first to put the Wild up 2-0. Justin Sourdif got the Capitals on the board with just six seconds left in the second, but they got no closer.
rows.calls: Three of four preview calls held

rows.head: Who’s in net for the Oilers?
rows.story: The Rangers are on a three-game losing streak. The Oilers have won two in a row, the last a 4-0 rout of the Islanders. Going in, the Oil are first in the Pacific (second in the NHL) and the Rangers fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 19th).

rows.head: Jensen meets his old team
rows.story: The Senators (9-5-1) beat San Jose 5-1 last night, while the Ducks (5-7-1) lost 7-6 to Buffalo on Thursday. Going in, the Sens are third in the Atlantic (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Ducks sixth in the Pacific (tied for 26th). The Senators’ record (.633) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.563), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games.

rows.note: Red Wings PP vs. Panthers PK
rows.head: DeBrincat’s favorite opponent
rows.story: The Panthers have won three straight, while the Red Wings (6-5-3) lost 5-4 to St. Louis on Saturday. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Red Wings last (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Panthers fifth (tied for eighth).

rows.head: The Flames are going to let it fly
rows.story: The Flames (6-8-0) lost 5-2 to Colorado on Saturday, and the Sharks (7-7-1) lost 5-1 to Ottawa the same night. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Flames fifth (tied for 24th in the NHL) and the Sharks fourth (tied for 19th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.

rows.head: Marner’s favorite opponent
rows.story: The Golden Knights (9-5-1) lost 5-2 to New Jersey on Friday, while the Bruins (10-4-1) beat Chicago 5-4 in overtime on Saturday. Going in, the Knights are second in the Pacific (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Bruins first in the Atlantic (fourth). The Golden Knights have played better than their record (.633) says: their chances are worth about .691, and their goaltending has held them back.

rows.head: The Avalanche should tilt the ice
rows.story: The Blackhawks (4-9-1) lost 5-4 in overtime to Boston on Saturday, while the Avalanche have won two in a row. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Avalanche third (tied for 13th in the NHL) and the Blackhawks last (31st). The Avalanche’s record (.607) is about what their chances are worth.

rows.head: Who’s in net for the Rangers?
rows.story: The Rangers are on a three-game losing streak, while the Blues have won two in a row. Going in, the Blues are fifth in the Central (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Rangers fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 19th). The Blues have played better than their record (.536) says: their chances are worth about .593, and their goaltending has held them back.

rows.head: Who’s in net for the Oilers?
rows.story: The Devils (9-5-0) beat Vegas 5-2 on Friday. The Oilers have won two in a row, the last a 4-0 rout of the Islanders. Going in, the Oil are first in the Pacific (third in the NHL) and the Devils second in the Metropolitan (tied for eighth).

rows.head: Nichushkin meets his old team
rows.story: The Blue Jackets (5-7-0) lost 3-1 to Dallas on Saturday, while the Avalanche have won two in a row. The Avalanche played last night, and the Blue Jackets are rested. Going in, the Avalanche are third in the Central (tied for 13th in the NHL) and the Blue Jackets last in the Metropolitan (tied for 29th).

rows.head: Brink returns to Philadelphia
rows.story: The Wild (10-3-3) beat Washington 5-1 on Sunday, and the Flyers (4-8-4) beat Utah 6-3 the same night. Going in, the Wild are first in the Central (second in the NHL) and the Flyers seventh in the Metropolitan (tied for 24th). The Wild draw more penalties than they take (2nd) and leave the shooting to their forwards (3rd lowest), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (31st).

rows.head: Who blinks first?
rows.story: The Golden Knights won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-2 in Vegas on Oct 17. The Golden Knights (9-5-1) lost 5-2 to New Jersey on Friday, and the Penguins (5-7-2) lost 5-4 to Montréal on Saturday. The Golden Knights played last night, and the Penguins are rested.

rows.head: The Mammoth should tilt the ice
rows.story: The Mammoth won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-4 in Utah on Oct 13. The Mammoth (9-6-0) lost 6-3 to Philadelphia on Sunday, while the Maple Leafs (8-6-2) beat Vancouver 4-2 on Saturday. Going in, the Mammoth are second in the Central (tied for eighth in the NHL) and the Leafs sixth in the Atlantic (tied for eighth).

rows.head: The Jets are desperate for a win
rows.story: The Jets are winless in nine (0-7-2). The Canadiens are on a tear, five straight wins. The Canadiens won the teams’ first meeting this season, 2-1 in Winnipeg on Oct 25.

rows.head: The Red Wings played last night
rows.story: The Red Wings (6-5-3) lost 5-4 to St. Louis on Saturday, and the Lightning (8-3-2) lost 5-4 in a shootout to Nashville the same night. The Red Wings played last night, and the Bolts are rested.

rows.head: The Capitals can’t afford to take penalties
rows.story: The Stars (8-5-1) beat Columbus 3-1 on Saturday, while the Capitals (8-5-0) lost 5-1 to Minnesota on Sunday. Going in, the Stars are fourth in the Central (tied for 13th in the NHL) and the Caps third in the Metropolitan (tied for 17th). The Stars block more shots than anyone (1st) and play slow, tight games (lowest).

rows.head: Boeser’s favorite opponent
rows.story: The Canucks won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-5 in overtime in Anaheim on Oct 27. The Ducks (5-7-1) lost 7-6 to Buffalo on Thursday, and the Canucks (3-12-1) lost 4-2 to Toronto on Saturday. Going in, the Ducks are sixth in the Pacific (tied for 27th in the NHL) and the Canucks are last in the NHL.

rows.head: The Hurricanes are rolling
rows.story: The Predators (5-4-5) beat Tampa Bay 5-4 in a shootout on Saturday. The Hurricanes have won four straight, the last a 7-0 rout of Winnipeg. Going in, the Canes are first in the NHL and the Predators sixth in the Central (tied for 19th in the NHL).

standout.head: Jakob Chychrun blocked 6 shots
standout.sub: Only 14 other games this season have matched it. Blocked shots as the home scorer recorded them.
